title: The Conductor Developer
content: Software development is shifting from individual coding to orchestrating AI agents. While AI was initially framed as a productivity tool for writing code faster, the real bottleneck has become human attention. Great developers now resemble conductors directing multiple agents in parallel—providing context, evaluating outputs, and making iteration decisions—rather than musicians playing instruments themselves. This mirrors how executives manage energy amid constant context switching. The industry must now redesign engineering careers and training around attention management, prioritization, and cognitive load rather than individual execution.

content: On July 31, DeepSeek launched the public beta of its V4-Flash API, featuring significantly enhanced agent capabilities. The model achieved high scores across nine benchmark tests, including 82.7 on Terminal Bench and 76.7 on Cybergym, demonstrating strong performance in terminal operations, cybersecurity, and full-stack development. Notably, the model architecture remained unchanged from the preview version; the improvements came solely from refined post-training. The release includes native Responses API support for Codex compatibility. The upgrade applies only to the V4-Flash API, with V4-Pro and app interfaces unchanged.

title: 翁荔刚回OpenAI，Thinking Machines反手甩出新模型
content: Thinking Machines released Inkling-Small, a 276B-parameter MoE model with only 12B active parameters, outperforming its 975B predecessor Inkling and trillion-parameter rivals in benchmarks including ARC-AGI-2. The company achieved this through on-policy distillation followed by two weeks of agentic coding reinforcement learning. The smaller model significantly lowers deployment barriers, requiring modest hardware versus Inkling's 2TB minimum. The release came days after co-founder Weng Li returned to OpenAI, continuing a trend of departures that has seen four of six founders leave—three returning to OpenAI—yet the startup maintains rapid model release cadence despite talent drain.

title: 突发，GPT-5.6今起大降价
content: OpenAI reduced API prices for its GPT-5.6 models. Entry-level Luna dropped 80% to $0.20/$1.20 per million tokens (input/output); mid-tier Terra fell 20% to $2/$12; flagship Sol kept prices but added Fast mode at 2.5× speed for 2× cost. OpenAI said GPT-5.6 Sol helped optimize its own production GPU kernels and speculative decoding, cutting serving costs by 20% and improving token generation by over 15%. Subscription prices remain unchanged, but usage credits now stretch further. The sharpest cut to Luna targets cost-sensitive, high-frequency agent workflows.

title: 中层消失，Token狂热退潮，硅谷工程师眼里的「AI创业下半场」
content: Silicon Valley AI engineer Ma Peiyuan observes that the AI startup scene has entered a new phase. Talent preferences shifted toward generalist "polyglot" developers over specialists, with AI-native skills now outweighing years of experience. Organizations are flattening—Cognition operates with nearly no pure people managers, while tech giants are cutting middle management. The early "Token Maxxing" trend of maximizing AI usage is being reconsidered as costs mount, with companies now favoring blended "fusion mode" approaches combining cheaper and top-tier models. New infrastructure for monitoring AI agents and vertical applications handling "untrainable" complex processes represent emerging investment opportunities.

title: Stacked sessions and pull requests in the GitHub Copilot app
content: A developer modernized a decade-old personal React app using GitHub Copilot's stacked sessions and pull requests. After an initial failed attempt to one-shot the migration, they discovered they needed to work off an existing dev branch. Copilot seamlessly created a new session, closed the failed pull request, and ported styling changes. The developer then used stacked sessions to isolate react-bootstrap removal into a separate, dependent pull request branching off the first—forming an ordered chain of PRs targeting each other before eventually landing on main.

title: How Yahoo enhances search retargeting using Amazon Bedrock
content: Yahoo replaced its legacy Word2Vec and locality-sensitive hashing keyword expansion system with Amazon Bedrock-hosted large language models to enhance Search Retargeting in its Demand-Side Platform. The new generative AI approach, using Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2, produces semantically richer keyword expansions with up to 600 times higher expansion rates and five times greater audience reach. Guardrails including embedding-based similarity scoring and sensitive keyword filtering maintain quality and compliance. Amazon Bedrock's serverless access to multiple foundation models enabled rapid experimentation without infrastructure management.

title: Inference meta-monitoring for Amazon SageMaker AI endpoints with Amazon Quick
content: AWS proposes an inference meta-monitoring system for Amazon SageMaker AI endpoints using Amazon QuickSight and optional MLflow. The solution tracks prediction and data quality metrics through automated pipelines that detect model drift, integrate delayed ground truth labels, and generate performance dashboards. Architecture combines SageMaker AI, Athena, Lambda, EventBridge, and open-source Evidently AI. Five Athena Iceberg tables centralize data, with separate training and evaluation baselines enabling stable comparisons across model versions. A daily drift Lambda computes Jensen-Shannon distance metrics normalized to a scale of 0-10, with severity bands triggering SNS alerts. Pre-built QuickSight dashboards offer 32 visuals across model, data, and feature drift trends, including heatmaps and natural-language query support. The serverless design costs approximately $60 monthly with pay-per-use scaling.
